observation_summary: The test failed because the mock object created via @Spy did not have the expected name ('veryCoolSpy') in its error message, causing an assertion failure.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces a simple 'Mockito.spy(instance)' call with a more complex 'Mockito.mock(...)' configuration that explicitly sets the name using '.name(field.getName())'. This is a change in the procedural logic used to initialize the spy object, specifically correcting the method-level strategy for how the spy is constructed and named. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a simple value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object), but rather a correction to the internal implementation of the spy creation algorithm.
evidence_used: The fix replaces 'field.set(testClass, Mockito.spy(instance));' with a call that uses 'withSettings().name(field.getName())'.
The failing test expected the error message to contain the name 'veryCoolSpy'.
The fix explicitly adds the name to the mock settings during the spy initialization process.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While it involves initialization, the fix is not just setting a value but changing the entire construction procedure (algorithm) of the mock object to include naming metadata.
The capability to name a mock already existed; the fix simply ensures the spy initialization procedure utilizes this existing capability correctly.
